name: Gyaru makeover cafe

card.summary: A Shibuya-style cafe where staff in gyaru fashion offer hair and makeup makeovers so visitors can try the gyaru look.
card.note: Prices and hours reported by travel sources differ and may have changed.

quick.overview:
A gyaru makeover cafe is a themed cafe and bar staffed by gyaru, women in Japan's gal fashion subculture, where visitors can have hair and makeup done in the gyaru style. The best-known example is galcafe 10sion in Shibuya, Tokyo.

The appearance payoff is a one-off transformation into the look, with voluminous hair, dramatic eye makeup and false lashes, and a chance to learn the techniques from people who wear it daily.
quick.how: Visitors sit with gyaru staff, join workshops such as an 'Experience Gal Make-Up' session, and can be made over with hair and makeup and photographed, according to coverage of the cafe from 2012 to 2017. Staff speak casually rather than in formal honorifics.
quick.risks: There are no health risks specific to the service beyond ordinary cosmetics use. Kotaku noted in 2012 that some people online called it overpriced, and sources disagree on current pricing and hours.

lead: Gyaru is a Japanese fashion subculture, with roots in the 1970s and 1990s, associated with Shibuya, tanned or bright skin in some substyles, voluminous coloured hair, dramatic eye makeup with large false lashes and circle contacts [1]. Gyaru-themed cafes employ waitresses in gyaru attire who typically avoid formal speech, and galcafe 10sion is listed as one that offers gyaru makeovers [1].

Kotaku reported in May 2012 that the cafe, set in Shibuya rather than Akihabara, was built around the idea of seeing gals in their home district and offered free gal workshops, including one on gal makeup, for male and female visitors [2].

chain: Staff do hair and makeup in gyaru style
Visitor leaves with the look and photos
angle.text: The cafe lets visitors adopt the gyaru look in a single session, with makeup and hair done by experienced wearers of the style, and pick up techniques they can repeat themselves.

paras: Gyaru-themed cafes employ staff in gyaru dress, and the visitor experience includes socialising, photos and makeover services [1][2]. Related venues include Beauty Cafe by GirlsAward, which employs reader models, and the Ganguro Cafe in Shibuya, which closed in July 2018 [1].

Gyaru fashion spans substyles such as ganguro with deep tans and bleached hair, kogal, and hime gyaru with a pastel rococo look; since the Reiwa era makeup has trended lighter and softer [1]. Magazines such as egg, Popteen and Koakuma Ageha helped spread the look [1].

timeline.event: Kotaku reports on galcafe 10sion in Shibuya and its free gal makeup workshops [2].
The Ganguro Cafe in Shibuya closes [1].
